scope: Follow-up adaptation of the ACK accessory addition; the whole-driver candidate remains provisional pending bulk-I/O review.
changes: Each queued EP0 request owns a separate acc_dev reference and immutable request metadata. HID lookups acquire a HID kref under dev->lock. Queue failure and every completion, including errors, release those references exactly once. Setup retains its own reference if another CPU completes before usb_ep_queue returns. Native UDC contract promises exactly one completion only after successful queueing; actual hardware not tested.

HID list ownership, initialization ownership and EP0 ownership are separate references. Sleeping HID destruction runs on a release worker; each HID retains acc_dev until destruction. Initialization remains on new_hid_list so disconnect/replacement can mark it dead. A dead object is never republished; failed initialization is unlinked before final release. hid_parse_report errors propagate.

Retain existing descriptor limit 4096 and ID range 1..32. New cap 64 counts every allocated HID including dead, in-flight and deferred-release objects. Replacement at this cap returns EBUSY until cleanup finishes; allocation failure leaves the original ID intact. This is intentional bounded backpressure, not a claim of unchanged behavior for an unlimited replacement stream.

Each acc_dev holds a device-model reference for event workers and HID parents. Cleanup closes new lookup/control producers, drains notifications before misc deregistration, retires all HID lists, and drains registration work. Existing EP0 references keep objects alive until completion; stale completions cannot restart work after closing. The final instance worker drops the stable device reference after draining remaining work. Configfs instance storage is freed.
security: All changes are inside the ACK-added driver. Native HID core, USB core and LTS fixes remain unchanged. Allocation caps mitigate host-driven growth; reference ownership prevents completion use-after-free and detached initialization escaping disconnect. Raw HID input still enters native quiescing. This does not certify bulk request/read/write teardown, which remains under review.
validation: 31 extracted ASan/UBSan host scenarios pass and leave no allocations. Four explicitly fault-injected variants fail (not executions of the original full ACK driver). Existing eight singleton and 24 native-input model cases also pass after updating modeled structures. Kernel build 153 passed with 145 module signatures/tables verified; no real USB, kernel races, HID BPF or emulator execution.

native_contracts.finding: usb_ep_queue exactly-once successful completion contract; completion may run on another CPU before queuing CPU finishes. usb_ep_dequeue is asynchronous; usb_ep_disable completes pending requests before return, with no other task allowed to use endpoint.
hid_destroy_device removes driver/device before dropping device reference; native input quiescing retained.
